newsitem.title: CZECH REPUBLIC: Czech PM Klaus says stable crown policies continue.
newsitem.headline: Czech PM Klaus says stable crown policies continue.

text.p: Czech Prime Minister Vaclav Klaus on Monday said his government was still committed to policies that will keep the crown currency stable.

"Together with the central bank, we are ready to continue in the policy of a stable exchange rate which gave our business sector so many stable points in the turbulent waters of liberalisation," Klaus told an international engineering conference.

"In this phase, the policy of a stable exchange rate is a good tool, stimulating the restructuring of privatised companies, and it stimulates higher effectiveness and competitiveness on foreign markets," he said.
In his opening address to the conference in the city of Brno, the conservative Prime Minister said that as a result, interest rates would remain high, at least over the short term.
"The best way to face this problem is a decline in inflation, and...an improvement of cautiousness of commercial banks and through that a decrease in the share of risky loans," he said.
"(But) a short-term solution of this important problem (high interest rates)...doesn't exist," he said.
Klaus also said better supervision of banks by the central bank would help the credit environment.
Czech inflation has been one of the lowest in the region, but after dropping below double digits last year, it has remained stubbornly high at around nine percent annually.
The central bank discount rate currently stands at 10.5 percent, while its last resort lending facility for banks, the Lombard rate, is 14 percent.
Klaus said abnormally low unemployment, stuck at around three percent, has kept the labour pool weak and the ensuing wage pressure was inflationary.
"We consider the problems caused by the insufficient pool of labour as serious," he said.
He also said the ballooning current account deficit was still financeable, though his government was watching its development closely.
